compiler_deviation_note: Original llama-research-v2 was built with x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++-posix (GCC) 13-posix. This build used mingw-w64 GCC 10.3.0-posix (Ubuntu 22.04 'jammy' universe) because the build environment has no root access to add a newer Ubuntu release pocket; GCC 13 mingw-w64 packages were not obtainable here. The MinGW-w64 header/runtime package used is also an older version (8.0.0, 2020) than whatever shipped with the GCC13 toolchain used for llama-research-v2; this required adding -D_WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00 -DWINVER=0x0A00 to the compile flags so that cpp-httplib's use of CreateFile2/WSAPoll/inet_pton/POLLIN/POLLOUT resolves against these older mingw-w64 headers (the newer header package presumably already defaults high enough; this define makes the older one behave the same way). This is disclosed as a build-environment deviation, not a silent substitution. It affects only the C/C++ toolchain and the Windows-API feature-level macro used by one vendored HTTP library; it does not touch, and could not touch, any R2-12 frozen parameter, retention-policy decision, or benchmark protocol -- none of which are compiled conditionally on _WIN32_WINNT. The resulting llama-server.exe links only against the same five system DLLs as the original (ADVAPI32, KERNEL32, SHELL32, WS2_32, msvcrt), confirming the same static-linked, no-OpenMP build shape as llama-research-v2.
built_on: Argine2 build container (Linux), cross-compiled. MinGW-w64 toolchain + cmake/ninja obtained without root via 'apt-get download' + 'dpkg-deb -x' into a user-owned prefix under ~/toolchain/; invoked via GCC_EXEC_PREFIX / --sysroot / -B compiler-driver overrides and LD_LIBRARY_PATH for cmake's own shared-library deps. No system install, no bind mounts, no elevated privileges of any kind.
runtime_tested_note: Not executed in this Linux build environment (it is a Windows PE32+ binary). Verified here only by static inspection: objdump import-table DLL names, and 'strings' search for the compiled-in retention-policy provenance line and env-var names (see verification log). Live confirmation that the startup line 'argine: retention policy attiva: ...' is actually printed before any real-model request is accepted must happen on the real Windows host -- this is R2-12 Phase C requirement #10 and is explicitly left to the user's own next run, not claimed here.
